Name: BlueHour
Author: stanzhang
Description:
[b]To the AI-generated police:[/b]
[b]
I don’t know who added the AI-generated tag to all of my mods just because the cover image of this mod used AI-generated artwork.
My music and my code are all original work created by me personally.
The reason I create these things and share them is because I love this game, and I also love the modding community.
But from the bottom of my heart, I deeply, deeply dislike this kind of AI content policing.
When I first started making mods, I was happy. And I know very well that making mods does not really bring any income. They are free things shared with everyone, hopefully to bring people some joy.
But on Nexus, I have met the most disgusting group of people I have ever encountered here: people like you.[/b]

[b]At first, they saw a lot of low-quality AI-generated content, and that part is understandable. A lot of AI content is indeed ugly, lazy, repetitive, and badly made. But then they turned that experience into a stereotype: AI-generated equals garbage.
From that point on, they stopped caring whether a specific work is actually good or bad. Once they recognize that something was made with AI, or even just assisted by AI, they immediately label it as trash.[/b]
[b]They have finally found a socially acceptable target onto which they can project their stereotypes, disgust, moral superiority, and desire for collective aggression.[/b]
[b]The reason they can do this so aggressively is that AI is not a human being. If they applied the same kind of stereotype-based hatred to any race, group of people, culture, or even animals like cats or dogs, they would be attacked immediately. But because the target is “AI,” they finally have a socially acceptable outlet for this kind of prejudice.[/b]
[b]So in the end, it is no longer about whether the work looks bad. It is about the label. They see “AI,” and then they decide they hate it.[/b]
[b]The irony is that many of the loudest people in this debate are not even creators themselves. They are not the ones actually making things.[/b]
[b]And from that position of moral superiority, they feel entitled to casually and brutally label the hard work of creators who are doing all of this for free.[/b]

[b][color=#ff0000]And that inevitably raises a simple question about Nexus Mods as a platform: was it built by the creators who make mods for free, or by the self-appointed moral judges who do nothing but label and police other people’s work?[/color][/b]
[b]
Please stay away from me.
Thank you for your cooperation.[/b]

[b]Description[/b]
A few days ago, the author of this mod decided to try something new outside of making mods: writing a piece of music.

The idea was simple—a short track inspired by the blue hour at the beach, that brief moment in the evening when the sun is gone but the sky still holds onto its last traces of blue.

The reality, however, was much less simple.

Writing melodies is hard.

Very hard.

After spending far too much time listening to the same eight bars on repeat and repeatedly failing to write a ninth one, the author suddenly had a strange idea:

What if this unfinished little piece didn’t need a ninth bar at all?

What if it belonged somewhere else?

While listening to those same eight bars over and over again, he realized that the mood felt surprisingly similar to Stardew Valley. The electric piano, the simplicity, the sense of calm—it felt like it could already exist somewhere in Pelican Town.

And so this mod was born.

Blue Hour adds that short piece of music to the beach after 6 PM.

[b][u]Some songs become albums.[/u][/b]
[u][b]
This one became a Stardew Valley mod.[/b][/u]



[b]几天前，这个 Mod 的作者决定尝试一些制作 Mod 之外的新东西：写一段音乐。
最初的想法很简单——写一首短曲，灵感来自海边的蓝色时刻，也就是傍晚太阳落下之后，天空却还残留着最后一抹蓝色的短暂时间。
但现实显然没有那么简单。
写旋律很难。
非常难。
在花了太多时间反复听同样的八个小节，并一次又一次写不出第九小节之后，作者突然产生了一个奇怪的想法：
如果这段未完成的小曲子，根本不需要第九小节呢？
如果它本来就属于另一个地方呢？
在一遍又一遍听着那八个小节的时候，他意识到，这段音乐的情绪和《星露谷物语》意外地相似。电钢琴、简单的旋律、平静的感觉——它听起来就像是本来就可以存在于鹈鹕镇的某个地方。
于是，这个 Mod 就这样诞生了。
Blue Hour 会在每天晚上 6 点之后，为海边加入这段短短的音乐。
有些歌会变成专辑。
而这一首，变成了一个《星露谷物语》Mod。[/b]

Requirements
- SMAPI 4.5.2 or newer
- Stardew Valley 1.6+

Installation
1. Install SMAPI.
2. Extract the BlueHour folder into your Mods directory.
3. Launch the game with SMAPI.
4. Visit the beach after 6 PM.

Main Features
- Plays a custom original music track at the beach after 6 PM.
- Designed specifically for evening fishing and quiet beach walks.
- Includes an original composition created by the mod author.

ps：

Blue Hour was inspired by a place I can’t seem to forget.
Many summers ago, I often visited a small seaside city. I still remember the smell of the sea breeze, the distant ships on the horizon, and the way the sky slowly turned blue after sunset.
Years have passed. People change. Life changes.
But somehow, that coastline has stayed with me.
This song is not about a person. It is about a moment, a season, and a feeling that never completely left.
It is also the first piece of music I have ever truly created.
To my surprise, I found exactly what I was looking for in just two days.
I enjoyed every moment of making it, and I still enjoy listening to it now.
I hope you will too.
— Stan
